qs.q: A 58-year-old stem cell transplant recipient with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis experiences persistent disease despite voriconazole therapy. Which intravenous antifungal drug is most appropriate to add or substitute?
qs.e: Caspofungin is an echinocandin that inhibits beta-1,3-glucan synthase and is indicated for azole-refractory invasive aspergillosis. Fluconazole lacks reliable activity against Aspergillus species entirely.

qs.q: A gardener pricks her finger on a rose thorn, developing a subcutaneous nodule that ulcerates, followed by the appearance of a chain of similar nodules along the lymphatic drainage tract. Which antifungal drug is the standard drug of choice for treating this infection?
qs.e: Itraconazole is the drug of choice for treating cutaneous and lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix schenckii. Amphotericin B is generally reserved for severe systemic mycoses or initial disseminated phases.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Fundamentals: Fungi, Antifungal Drugs & More: MCQs

qs.q: Which antifungal drug class exerts its primary pharmacologic target by binding to cell membrane ergosterol?
qs.e: Amphotericin B targets cell membrane ergosterol to disrupt fungal cellular integrity. Echinocandins target cell wall glucans, whereas flucytosine and griseofulvin target nucleic acids and microtubules.
qs.s: Medical Virology: Adenoviruses, Hemorrhagic Fever & Viral Receptors: MCQs

qs.q: Which antifungal drug class exerts its primary mechanism of action by disrupting the mitotic spindle and inhibiting fungal mitosis?
qs.e: Griseofulvin uniquely functions by disrupting the mitotic spindle and inhibiting fungal mitosis. Caspofungin acts instead by inhibiting fungal cell wall synthesis.
qs.s: Mycology Revision: Fungal Infections, Histoplasmosis & Cryptococcosis: MCQs

qs.q: An antifungal drug such as Miconazole inhibits proper formation of which cellular component?
o: Peptidoglycan in the fungal cell wall
Chitin in the fungal cell wall
qs.e: Azoles like miconazole block ergosterol synthesis, which is a crucial component of fungal plasma membranes, disrupting membrane formation and integrity.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - October 9, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which of the following antifungal drugs primarily inhibits the proper formation of ergosterol, a crucial component of the fungal cell membrane?
qs.e: Azole antifungals like miconazole block ergosterol synthesis by inhibiting fungal cytochrome P450-dependent enzymes, leading to disruption of plasma membrane integrity and function.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A component of the cell membrane of most fungi that is a primary target for several antifungal drugs is:
qs.e: Ergosterol is the main sterol found in the cell membrane of most fungi, analogous to cholesterol in mammalian cells. It is a critical target for many antifungal drugs, including azoles (which inhibit its synthesis) and polyenes (which bind to it).
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: The primary mechanism of action for antifungal drugs in the echinocandin class (e.g., caspofungin) is:
o: Inhibits synthesis of β‑(1,3)‑glucan in the cell wall.
Binds to ergosterol within the cell membrane.
qs.e: Echinocandins inhibit the synthesis of β-(1,3)-D-glucan, a crucial polysaccharide component of the fungal cell wall. This leads to osmotic instability and cell lysis, making them fungicidal against most Candida species.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
